item.mechanism: The alternating soft fcc and hard B2 phases create a composite structure where hard B2 phases (including nanoscale precipitates) pin dislocation movement as they pass through soft fcc phases, resulting in significant work hardening and high ductility despite high strength.
item.system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) with fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure
item.operating_conditions: As-cast state; room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 700°C; tensile loading
item.supporting_observation: The alloy exhibited ultra-high strain hardening behavior with a proof stress of 75 MPa reaching a fracture stress close to 1.2 GPa at room temperature, maintaining high strength and ductility up to 700°C.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is proposed for the specific fine lamellar eutectic structure; the authors note the mechanism for the low elastic limit (proof stress) is still unclear at this stage.
item.alternatives_considered: Single-phased fcc HEAs (ductile but not strong) and single-phased bcc HEAs (strong but brittle); simple fcc/bcc combinations without proper structural design.
quotes: The very large strain hardening for the as-cast EHEA could originate from the fine regular lamellar structure that easily stores dislocations

When dislocations pass through soft fcc phases, these hard B2 phases, including the nanoscale B2-structured precipitates within the fcc phases, could pin the movement of dislocations and result in the significant work hardening phenomenon.

The proof stress is determined by shifting the linear elastic curve to 0.2% strain. We choose to not to call it the yield stress, as the mechanism for such a low elastic limit is still unclear at this stage.

item.mechanism: The eutectic solidification process produces near-equilibrium microstructures with low-energy phase boundaries and regular lamellar organization, which resist microstructural change at high temperatures and provide high rupture strength.
item.system: Eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) designed with the eutectic alloy concept
item.operating_conditions: High temperatures up to the reaction temperature; solidification state
item.supporting_observation: The as-cast EHEA possessed a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure with an inter-lamellar spacing of about 2 μm and showed excellent mechanical properties up to 700°C.
item.scope_limits: Requires the alloy to be at or near the eutectic composition to achieve the isothermal transformation and avoid solidification temperature ranges.
item.alternatives_considered: Non-eutectic HEAs which suffer from inferior castability and compositional segregation.
quotes: Eutectic alloys are also known to be good candidate high-temperature alloys, because the eutectic solidification structure has the following features: 1) near-equilibrium microstructures that resist change at temperatures as high as their reaction temperature
Since the eutectic reaction is an isothermal transformation and hence there exists no a solidification temperature range, both the segregation and shrinkage cavity can be alleviated.
The as-cast EHEA possessed a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, and showed an unprecedented combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature.

item.mechanism: Conventional casting of eutectic HEAs eliminates the need for expensive processing routes (like single crystal growth) while achieving a uniform microstructure, thereby overcoming the castability and segregation issues common to bulk HEAs.
item.operating_conditions: Vacuum induction melting at 1500°C pouring temperature; conventional casting method
item.supporting_observation: The bulk alloy exhibited excellent castability with few casting defects and a uniform fine lamellar microstructure, unlike other bulk HEAs.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 composition and the eutectic design strategy; not tested for non-eutectic HEAs.
item.alternatives_considered: Other bulk HEAs which have inferior castability and compositional segregation.
quotes: The bulk AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy exhibited an excellent castability with few casting defects, significantly differentiating with other bulk HEAs.
Even in such a bulk cast ingot, a uniform and fine lamellar microstructure characteristic of eutectic alloys was achieved.
The EHEA prepared using conventional casting and without subsequent processing can have such excellent mechanical properties is indeed groundbreaking.

item.mechanism: Thermomechanical treatments (specifically cold rolling) can further tune mechanical properties by increasing proof and fracture stress while maintaining decent ductility through work hardening.
item.operating_conditions: Cold rolling with 8% thickness reduction; room temperature tensile testing
item.supporting_observation: Cold rolling with 8% reduction increased the engineering proof stress to 275 MPa and fracture stress to 1145 MPa, while retaining 10.4% elongation.
item.scope_limits: The text notes this is a simple treatment; further optimization is needed for room-temperature and elevated temperature properties.
item.alternatives_considered: As-cast state properties which are already high but can be improved.
quotes: The mechanical properties of the as-cast EHEA can be further tuned by thermomechanical treatments.

A simple cold rolling with a thick reduction of 8% can increase the engineering/true proof stress and fracture stress to 275 MPa and 1145 MPa/1265 MPa, respectively, while remaining a decent ductility of 10.4%/9.9% in elongation.

The unprecedentedly large strain hardening and low yield stress (proof stress) give rise to the unique opportunity of this EHEA in producing ultrahigh strength components after large plastic deformation.

item.mechanism: The pseudo-binary nature of the alloy (NiAl-rich B2 phase and Co/Cr/Fe-rich fcc phase) allows for the design of a composite structure that balances the low ductility of NiAl with the high strength of the fcc phase.
item.system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA (regarded as a highly concentrated pseudo-binary NiAl/(Co, Cr, Fe) eutectic alloy)
item.operating_conditions: As-cast state; room temperature and high temperature (up to 700°C)
item.supporting_observation: The alloy exhibited a much higher fracture strength and simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature compared to NiAl or NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys.
item.scope_limits: Relies on the specific phase constitution of fcc and B2; the authors state the mechanism for the low elastic limit is unclear.
item.alternatives_considered: NiAl alloys which have low ductility at room temperature and low strength at high temperatures.
quotes: The current EHEA can be regarded as a highly concentrated pseudo-binary NiAl/(Co, Cr, Fe) eutectic alloy.
Compared to NiAl or NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys, the EHEA exhibited a much higher fracture strength, and more importantly, a simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature.

This novel strategy is promising to solve the problems inhibiting the engineering application of HEAs as high-temperature materials, including the inferior castability and compositional segregation, and the conflict between high fracture strength and high ductility.

item.mechanism: The low density of the EHEA (7.38 g/cm³) combined with its high strength and ductility makes it competitive with Ni-based superalloys, which typically have densities above 8.0 g/cm³.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 700°C
item.supporting_observation: The density was measured to be 7.38 g/cm³, much lower than Ni-based superalloys, while maintaining high strength up to 700°C.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 composition; further optimization is needed to maintain this density while enhancing properties.
item.alternatives_considered: Ni-based superalloys which have higher density.
quotes: It is stressed here that the density of this EHEA was measured to be 7.38 g/cm 3 , much lower than those of Ni-based superalloys typically with a density of above 8.0 g/cm 3 .

Further optimization of the room-temperature and elevated temperature properties while maintaining this relatively lower density, will certainly enable EHEAs to become competitive high-temperature alloys to Ni-based superalloys.
The higher strength of the EHEA over non-EHEAs can be kept at least to 700°C.

item.mechanism: The eutectic design strategy utilizes physicochemical properties (atomic radius, mixing enthalpy, valence electron concentration) and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations to pinpoint eutectic compositions in multi-component systems.
item.system: General class of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys (EHEAs)
item.operating_conditions: Alloy design and thermodynamic calculation phase
item.supporting_observation: The authors successfully designed the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy using this strategy, resulting in a uniform microstructure and balanced properties.
item.scope_limits: Requires reliable thermodynamics databases for HEAs to be established; relies on the assumption of a pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system.
item.alternatives_considered: Traditional physical metallurgy principles which may not easily predict eutectic behavior in high-entropy systems.
quotes: Further exploration of new EHEAs will be based on previous established physical metallurgy principles to design HEAs, utilizing physiochemical material properties including atomic radius, mixing enthalpy and valence electron concentration.
Eutectic alloys compositions can be pinpointed assuming a pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system, and then varying the concentration of one element systematically.

item.mechanism: The coupled growth of fcc and B2 phases during eutectic solidification creates a regular lamellar organization that acts as an in-situ composite, providing high rupture strength and stable defect structures.
item.supporting_observation: The XRD pattern showed an fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution, and the DSC curve showed only one melting event, evidencing the eutectic composition and coupled growth.
item.scope_limits: Dependent on the specific eutectic composition; the mechanism assumes the formation of the specific lamellar structure.
item.alternatives_considered: Non-eutectic solidification which leads to segregation and irregular microstructures.
quotes: The coupled grown two phases showed a clear compositional contrast, with the regions marked by A in Fig. 2b were rich in Co, Cr and Fe, while the regions marked by B were rich in Al and Ni.
The differential scanning calorimetric (DSC) curve given in Fig. 3b shows only one melting event, further evidencing the eutectic composition in this alloy.
Regular lamellar or rod-like eutectic organization, forming an in-situ composite.
